counterexamples.evidence: After the better move (31133025134544600550) c1r4 is Gray, so the opponent diagonal c4r1,c3r2,c2r3,c1r4 is dead and column 3 carries only the single major at c3r3 — no 7-shape. After the played move plus the opponent reply (311330251345446005530) column 3 shows major at c3r2 [GT] AND major at c3r3, the actual fork. L3's “coming no matter what you play here” is board-false on the after-best branch.

Calling each empty square “a single square completing your opponent's four-in-a-row line” is board-false; the only genuine single completing square for the opponent is c3r3 (row 3 holds opponent discs at c1r3, c2r3, c4r3).

Omitting it removed the only visual evidence of what column 1 buys.

counterexamples.evidence: All 3 servedExplanations give tempo as the cause (“more quickly”, “less effort”, “an extra turn”, “resolve faster”). The player who just played column 4 is never told the transferable idea: the opponent needs BOTH c1r4 and c3r2 for that diagonal, column 1 takes one of them, and conceding c1r4 stacks a second threat directly under the c3r3 threat they already had.
